items.headline: Bitcoin's Seven-Day Hashrate Climbs Back to 1 ZH/s
items.summary: Bitcoin's network hashrate has returned to the 1 zettahash per second level, meaning miners are again performing over one sextillion calculations each second. The excerpt notes this comes as miners continue securing the network and competing for newly minted bitcoin.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin’s 7-Day Hashrate Returns to 1 ZH/s After Nearly 8 Months

items.headline: US Bitcoin ETFs Post $138M Outflows; Zcash Keeps Inflows
items.summary: U.S. bitcoin ETFs recorded about $137.94 million in net outflows on Friday, closing a week marked by sharp swings between inflows and selling. Ether saw modest inflows, while Zcash and NEAR also drew fresh capital.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $138M as Zcash Extends 3-Day Inflow Streak

items.headline: Fed Week Sets Up Key Moves for Stocks, Bitcoin and DXY
items.summary: A busy week of central bank decisions and PCE inflation data comes alongside an $11 billion Bitcoin options expiry. The excerpt does not detail specific outcomes or expectations.
items.sourceTitle: Fed Week Puts Stocks, Bitcoin, and DXY on Collision Course Before $11 Billion Expiry

items.headline: Bitcoin Challenge Site Offers $2,000 to Hackers, Unclaimed So Far
items.summary: A website offering $2,000 in bitcoin to anyone who can steal it remains unclaimed. An independent review suggests the challenge may be practically impossible to crack.
items.sourceTitle: Website Dares Hackers to Steal Bitcoin as the Clock Keeps Ticking

items.headline: Six More Firms Object to Trading Their Shares as Tokens
items.summary: Twenty-two companies have now objected to their shares being traded on a planned tokenized stock venue run by OKX-ICE. Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit and others recently joined the opposition.
items.sourceTitle: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks

items.headline: Keystone customers claim breach exposed data that was supposed to be deleted
items.summary: Customers say a breach revealed information the hardware wallet maker had pledged to delete. Keystone has said it generally erases customer data 180 days after orders, though some X users have questioned that claim.
items.sourceTitle: Keystone customers say breach exposed data the hardware wallet maker promised to delete

items.headline: ECB official links digital euro to EU monetary sovereignty
items.summary: Piero Cipollone, an ECB official, says the bloc plans real-transaction tests in 2027 and a possible digital euro rollout as early as 2029. Both timelines depend on legislation expected this year.
items.sourceTitle: ECB official sees digital euro as key to protecting EU ‘sovereignty’

items.headline: Hyperliquid Leads Perps Market as HYPE Token Slides
items.summary: The HYPE token has fallen about 22% from its September peak near $98, even as the decentralized platform holds roughly $7.7 billion in open interest. Analysts note its market share in real-world asset trading is shrinking.
items.sourceTitle: Hyperliquid Still Rules the Perps Market, but HYPE Bulls Face Trouble

items.headline: Netanyahu suggests blockchain could help Israel evade possible sanctions
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said ahead of elections that the country could turn to blockchain and crypto to get around potential international sanctions. The idea drew criticism from opponents and the central bank governor.
items.sourceTitle: Netanyahu floats use of blockchain as solution to potential financial sanctions

items.headline: Bitcoin hashrate recovers to 1 ZH/s despite miners shifting toward AI
items.summary: Large public Bitcoin miners are reallocating capacity toward artificial intelligence, yet the network's hashrate is still rising. The seven-day average has reportedly returned to around the 1 ZH/s level.
items.sourceTitle: Miner Weekly: Bitcoin Hashrate Shrugs off the AI Unplug, Regaining 1 ZH/s Level

items.headline: Brazil's Securities Regulator Backs Mandatory Tokenization for Market Oversight
items.summary: CVM president Otto Lobo argued that required tokenization, paired with AI supervision, is needed to update surveillance methods that no longer keep pace with large fund structures. The regulator defended the approach as a tool for market monitoring.
items.sourceTitle: Brazil Pushes Mandatory Tokenization to Overhaul Market Tracking

items.headline: Heatbit Unveils Water Heater That Doubles as Bitcoin Miner
items.summary: Heatbit has launched the Bitwater, an $899 device that replaces a standard heating element with 20 mining chips. The product aims to let household water heaters also generate bitcoin.
items.sourceTitle: Heatbit’s New Water Heater Miner Turns Hot Showers Into Bitcoin

items.headline: Kraken parent Payward to buy Finnish owner of Saldo Bank
items.summary: Payward, the parent company of Kraken, agreed on Oct. 14 to acquire Saldo Finance Oy, which owns Lithuania's Saldo Bank. The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
items.sourceTitle: Kraken wants to be your bank, but who will protect your money?

items.headline: Ripple Legal Chief Warns of Investor Losses in New Token Sales
items.summary: Ripple's legal chief Stuart Alderoty is urging clearer project commitments and issuer accountability over losses in new crypto offerings. His remarks come as the SEC weighs new fundraising rules.
items.sourceTitle: Ripple Legal Chief Raises Alarm Over Losses in New Crypto Offerings

items.headline: Real World Assets explained: what RWA means in crypto
items.summary: An explainer on real world assets (RWA), a term covering traditional assets represented on blockchains. The source excerpt is brief, so details beyond the basic definition are not provided.
items.sourceTitle: Real World Assets explained: what RWA really are - CryptoTicker

items.headline: Electrum Patch Fixes Flaw Used to Steal Bitcoin via Fee Bumps
items.summary: A malicious wallet server could swap a legitimate payment for a thief's transaction and wait for the owner's approval. Electrum's latest security update closes the loophole after attackers exploited it and stole funds.
items.sourceTitle: Electrum Wallet Attack Hid Bitcoin Theft Behind a Fee Increase

items.headline: Circle launches USDC auctions letting institutions earn redemption fee rebates
items.summary: Circle's new USDC auctions allow eligible institutions to collect rebates funded by matched redeemers. Redeemers' auction fees are capped at the Express rate.
items.sourceTitle: Circle’s new USDC auctions let institutions collect the fees others pay to cash out

items.headline: Ethereum sees large exchange outflow, mirroring pre-June rebound signal
items.summary: Ethereum recorded its largest net outflow from exchanges in over four months, according to Santiment data. The same pattern appeared before a rebound in June, though US spot Ethereum funds have seen notable outflows this October.
items.sourceTitle: Ethereum Flashes Same Signal That Triggered June’s Rebound

items.headline: Arthur Hayes closes out crypto trades, on-chain data shows about $26 million sold
items.summary: Arthur Hayes has exited Maelstrom's directional crypto positions, with analysts tracking roughly $26 million in token sales. Hayes reportedly cited macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty as the reason for taking profits on Ethereum, Ethena, Uniswap and other tokens.
items.sourceTitle: Arthur Hayes exits crypto trading positions as analysts track $26 million in sales

items.headline: NYSE parent backs round-the-clock tokenized stock trading
items.summary: The owner of the New York Stock Exchange is reportedly supporting stock tokens that would let people trade shares at any time. The move is framed as a response to growing demand for always-on trading seen in crypto and other tokenized assets.
items.sourceTitle: NYSE’s owner is backing 24/7 stock tokens without Wall Street’s usual price rules

items.headline: Strategy and Strive weigh bitcoin purchases against preferred dividend payments
items.summary: Preferred stock has funded nearly 136,000 bitcoin purchases for Strategy and Strive. Analysts expect this funding channel to complement the larger ETF market.
items.sourceTitle: Strategy, Strive face balancing act between bitcoin buying and preferred stock dividends

items.headline: Bitcoin dips under $80,000 as $200M in leveraged positions close
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Saturday, with over $200 million in crypto positions liquidated within an hour, most of them long bets. Ethereum also declined, and the total crypto market capitalisation dropped 4.06% over 24 hours.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Loses $80,000 as $200 Million in Leverage Unwinds in an Hour

items.headline: Bitcoin Whipsaws as Most Altcoins Slide Lower
items.summary: Bitcoin has swung between roughly $80,000 and $84,000 during October, with each rebound fading quickly. The excerpt suggests the weakness runs deeper across the wider token market than Bitcoin's price shows.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Keeps Reversing. Why Are 80% of Crypto Tokens Falling?

items.headline: Bitcoin dips below $80,000 amid Middle East evacuation news
items.summary: Bitcoin has fallen to its lowest level in over a month, dropping below $80,000 over the weekend. The decline coincides with U.S. evacuations linked to the Middle East.
items.sourceTitle: Crypto under weekend pressure, bitcoin slides below $80,000 on U.S. Middle East evacuations

items.headline: Big Firms' Opposition to Tokenized Stocks May Not Be Decisive
items.summary: Several major companies, including McDonald's, Microsoft and Google, objected to being listed on a new tokenized securities venue under an SEC innovation exemption. Commentary suggests the pushback may reflect issuer caution rather than a broad rejection of tokenization.
items.sourceTitle: Why McDonalds, Microsoft and Google saying no to tokenized stocks isn't a dealbreaker

items.headline: Argentine judge closes criminal case against Milei over LIBRA token
items.summary: A judge found that President Milei's promotion of the LIBRA memecoin did not amount to fraud, even though his backing drew attention to the token. The token has since crashed.
items.sourceTitle: Argentina drops criminal probe into President Milei over crashed memecoin LIBRA

items.headline: Wealthy Bitcoin holders shift toward loans and yield products
items.summary: Long-term investors are increasingly borrowing against their bitcoin and seeking income to grow their BTC holdings, according to Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin’s wealthy holders turning to loans and yield as investment habits mature: Xapo CEO

items.headline: HSBC Rolls Out Hong Kong Dollar Stablecoin Within PayMe App
items.summary: HSBC has launched its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin inside the PayMe app, a move that tests whether a bank-issued token can serve as everyday money.
items.sourceTitle: Hong Kong’s Biggest Bank Puts a Stablecoin in 3 Million Wallets

items.headline: Arthur Hayes Sells About $22M in Crypto, Expects Market Pain
items.summary: Arthur Hayes, chief investment officer of Maelstrom, has sold roughly $22.28 million in crypto from the firm's directional book. He confirmed the exit on X and said he plans to stay out of the market.
items.sourceTitle: Arthur Hayes Dumps $22 Million in Crypto, Warns of More Pain

items.headline: Apex Group CEO says stalled U.S. Clarity Act favors Asia, Middle East
items.summary: Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes argued that the U.S. Clarity Act's failure could push digital asset firms toward faster-moving jurisdictions in Asia and the Middle East.
items.sourceTitle: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO

items.headline: Senator seeks records on Tether payments to ex-adviser's firm
items.summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal, the top Democrat on a Senate investigations subcommittee, has requested records on stablecoin issuer Tether's reported payments to Nxum, a consulting firm co-founded by Bo Hines, a former White House crypto adviser.
items.sourceTitle: Senator probes Tether’s reported $6 million payments to ex-White House crypto adviser’s firm

items.headline: Franklin Templeton moves $150M in fund shares onto XRP Ledger
items.summary: Franklin Templeton added about $150 million in fund tokens to the XRP Ledger through two subscriptions on Thursday, nearly quadrupling its existing tokens on the network. All of them landed in a single wallet.
items.sourceTitle: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million in fund shares to XRP Ledger, all in one wallet

items.headline: OCC stablecoin rule changes redemption timing and bank obligations
items.summary: A new OCC rule for stablecoin issuers sets how the two-business-day redemption limit ends, with bank availability assessed separately. The excerpt gives few further details.
items.sourceTitle: New OCC stablecoin rule resets redemptions, and banks face big shifts

items.headline: Wells Fargo and Five Others Oppose OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Plan
items.summary: Reportedly, Wells Fargo and five other firms have objected to the OKX-ICE joint venture's proposed tokenized stock platform. The objections were filed under the SEC's innovation exemption.
items.sourceTitle: Wells Fargo and five others object to OKX-ICE tokenized stock listings: Report

items.headline: New York Seeks $1.37B Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Operators
items.summary: New York's attorney general is asking a court to order the operators of a crypto Ponzi scheme to repay investors, with interest. The alleged frauds took more than $1.1 billion from investors.
items.sourceTitle: NY Seeks $1.37 Billion Judgment Against Operators of NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Scheme

items.headline: Blockstream Starts Institutional Consulting Arm and Opens Lugano Office
items.summary: Blockstream plans to offer its engineering expertise to banks and asset managers from a new office in Lugano, Switzerland.
items.sourceTitle: Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office

items.headline: UK regulator says some crypto apps may need licences for automated routing
items.summary: The FCA's proposed guidance distinguishes between technical access and substantive involvement in transactions, as firms prepare for the UK's crypto regime starting October 2027.
items.sourceTitle: UK’s FCA says crypto apps may need licenses when algorithms choose trade routes

items.headline: Senator Blumenthal Seeks Tether Records on Payments to Nxum
items.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal has requested Tether's records concerning payments made to Nxum, a firm co-owned by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.
items.sourceTitle: Senate Democrat Probes Tether Payments to Ex-White House Crypto Adviser’s Firm

items.headline: SEC Lists AI Superintelligence and Tokenization Among Market Risks
items.summary: The SEC's Division of Examinations has named advanced technologies such as superintelligence, alongside tokenization risks, as areas of focus. The excerpt is brief and gives no further detail.
items.sourceTitle: SEC Flags AI 'Super Intelligence' and Tokenization as Systemic Market Risks

items.headline: Initia pauses its blockchain after reported exploit
items.summary: The Initia network suspended its layer-1 chain and rollups after security researchers flagged unauthorized token minting and asset transfers to Ethereum. The reported losses are said to exceed $2.6 million.
items.sourceTitle: Initia halts blockchain after exploit reportedly drains over $2.6M

items.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs see $635M outflows as BTC nears cost basis
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $635 million in net outflows on Thursday, the largest daily outflow since June 25, as bitcoin traded near the estimated cost basis of the funds' holdings. The withdrawals reversed nearly 60% of the inflows from the prior three sessions.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin ETFs shed $635 million as BTC tests their holdings’ estimated $81,500 cost basis

items.headline: Bitcoin Core Updates Security Policy Amid AI-Driven Bug Discovery
items.summary: Bitcoin Core developers will now backport fixes and release updates immediately for flaws considered easily discoverable, dropping long embargo periods. The change responds to bugs that an attacker could find with a single AI prompt.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Core Rewrites Its Security Policy for a World Where AI Finds Bugs in One Prompt

items.headline: Bitcoin Core Shortens Disclosure Timelines for AI-Discoverable Bugs
items.summary: Bitcoin Core will now fast-track fixes and disclosures for vulnerabilities that AI tools can easily rediscover, moving away from long embargo periods. The change applies to those bugs.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin Core Ends Long Embargoes for Bugs AI Can Rediscover

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs See Large Outflows After Oil Price Jump
items.summary: Bitcoin ETFs reportedly lost more than $635 million in a single day, after investors who had been buying all week reversed course on Thursday. The excerpt does not give further detail on the cause.
items.sourceTitle: Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike
